scenes.tts: Does a taste field in cortex do anything? And can a mouse know a taste, but stop wanting it?
scenes.visual: Title card: Opening the Package. Then insular cortex drawn from the side, with a question on screen.
scenes.narration: Does a taste field in cortex do anything? And can a mouse know a taste, but stop wanting it?

scenes.tts: In anaesthetized mice, one study reported separate fields for sweet, bitter, umami and sodium.
scenes.visual: Four separate coloured patches labelled sweet, bitter, umami, sodium. Label: anaesthetized mice, Chen and colleagues, 2011.
scenes.narration: In anaesthetized mice, one study reported separate fields for sweet, bitter, umami and sodium.

scenes.tts: Fields would matter more if they did something. Peng and colleagues made the fields respond to light, in awake mice.
scenes.visual: A fibre-optic light above the sweet and bitter fields. On-screen: Peng and colleagues, 2015; channelrhodopsin.
scenes.narration: Fields would matter more if they did something. Peng and colleagues made the fields respond to light, in awake mice.

scenes.tts: Light on the sweet field drove attraction. Light on the bitter field drove aversion. That is the value half.
scenes.visual: Sweet field lit: the mouse approaches. Bitter field lit: the mouse retreats. Label: value.
scenes.narration: Light on the sweet field drove attraction. Light on the bitter field drove aversion. That is the value half.

scenes.tts: To test identity, they trained mice to respond to bitter, and to hold back for sweet.
scenes.visual: A go and no-go task: bitter, the mouse responds; sweet, the mouse withholds.
scenes.narration: To test identity, they trained mice to respond to bitter, and to hold back for sweet.

scenes.tts: Why set the task against the mouse's own preference?
scenes.visual: Question on screen beside the go and no-go trials.
scenes.narration: Why set the task against the mouse's own preference?

scenes.tts: So the mouse cannot just follow its liking. But it could still learn a rule, such as respond to the unpleasant one.
scenes.visual: A crossed-out heart beside the sweet trial. Then a small note: loophole, a learned rule.
scenes.narration: So the mouse cannot just follow its liking. But it could still learn a rule, such as respond to the unpleasant one.

scenes.tts: So the team added controls. Trained mice judged new sweet and bitter chemicals with similar accuracy.
scenes.visual: Control card one: novel tastants, judged with similar accuracy.
scenes.narration: So the team added controls. Trained mice judged new sweet and bitter chemicals with similar accuracy.

scenes.tts: In one version, low salt, which mice like, shared the bitter answer. Liking alone could not solve that.
scenes.visual: Control card two: low salt (attractive) on the same go branch as bitter. Label: liking alone cannot solve this.
scenes.narration: In one version, low salt, which mice like, shared the bitter answer. Liking alone could not solve that.

scenes.tts: Blocking either field impaired recognition of its taste. Recognition recovered after the drug washed out.
scenes.visual: Table row fills in: block a field, recognition of that taste impaired, recovers on washout.
scenes.narration: Blocking either field impaired recognition of its taste. Recognition recovered after the drug washed out.

scenes.tts: Is there a tidy map, then? That is disputed. In alert, licking mice, another study found distributed responses.
scenes.visual: The tidy coloured fields fade and dissolve into scattered responding cells. Label: alert, licking mice, 2021. Stamp: map not settled.
scenes.narration: Is there a tidy map, then? That is disputed. In alert, licking mice, another study found distributed responses.

scenes.tts: Next, Wang and colleagues traced the two fields to different parts of the amygdala.
scenes.visual: Projections drawn from the sweet field and the bitter field to two different parts of the amygdala. On-screen: Wang and colleagues, 2018.
scenes.narration: Next, Wang and colleagues traced the two fields to different parts of the amygdala.

scenes.tts: Then they silenced the amygdala.
scenes.visual: The amygdala greys out. The manipulation table shows its last row with two question marks.
scenes.narration: Then they silenced the amygdala.

scenes.tts: What survives: recognizing the taste, or the pull toward the sweet field?
scenes.visual: The two empty cells pulse: trained recognition, and attraction to light on the sweet field.
scenes.narration: What survives: recognizing the taste, or the pull toward the sweet field?

scenes.tts: Recognition stayed. The mice still reported sweet and bitter correctly. But the attraction to sweet-field light was abolished.
scenes.visual: Last row fills in: recognition intact; attraction abolished.
scenes.narration: Recognition stayed. The mice still reported sweet and bitter correctly. But the attraction to sweet-field light was abolished.

scenes.tts: So identity and value can be pulled apart, in these assays and with this silencing method.
scenes.visual: The package icon opens; the label stays, the arrow drops away. Label: in these assays.
scenes.narration: So identity and value can be pulled apart, in these assays and with this silencing method.

scenes.tts: The pattern is simple. Manipulate one stage, measure two behaviours, and see which one moves.
scenes.visual: Three-step card: manipulate one stage; measure recognition and attraction; see which one moves.
scenes.narration: The pattern is simple. Manipulate one stage, measure two behaviours, and see which one moves.

scenes.tts: Value also changes with need. A sodium-depleted animal drinks salt concentrations it would normally reject.
scenes.visual: A mouse after sodium depletion drinking eagerly from a salt bottle it would normally avoid.
scenes.narration: Value also changes with need. A sodium-depleted animal drinks salt concentrations it would normally reject.

scenes.tts: The salt is the same. What changes, in these assays, is how much the animal wants it.
scenes.visual: The salt label stays fixed; the value arrow lengthens. Label: behavioural assays.
scenes.narration: The salt is the same. What changes, in these assays, is how much the animal wants it.

scenes.tts: Keep the scope. These are mouse assays. They do not show that value is computed only in the amygdala.
scenes.visual: Scope card: mouse assays; value not computed only in the amygdala.
scenes.narration: Keep the scope. These are mouse assays. They do not show that value is computed only in the amygdala.

scenes.tts: In decerebrate rats, brainstem circuits still support innate acceptance and rejection. And learning shapes value too.
scenes.visual: The brainstem lights up, with accept and reject icons. On-screen: rats; taste-reactivity tests; Grill and Norgren, 1978. A small learning icon is added beside the value arrow.
scenes.narration: In decerebrate rats, brainstem circuits still support innate acceptance and rejection. And learning shapes value too.

scenes.tts: In these mouse experiments, silencing the amygdala removed the attraction and spared trained recognition.
scenes.visual: Takeaway card: two behavioural readouts side by side, Recognition (stays lit) and Attraction (fades), under the label Amygdala silenced. Label: in these mouse assays.
scenes.narration: In these mouse experiments, silencing the amygdala removed the attraction and spared trained recognition.
